definitions.basic: The 'reference' is the data that contains the source of truth of the prediction, and the 'candidate' is the prediction that was calculated and we want to compare with the 'reference'. To make the comparison, we divide both the reference and candidate into 'chromosome-strand-group', each chromosome-strand-group contains data from a given chromosome in a given strand.
definitions.forward, reverse, and general: The data can be divided into data that comes from one of the strands, or both. If the data has no filtered, thus coming from both forward or reverse strand it recieves the 'general' definition, otherwise it recieves 'forward' or 'reverse' accordingly.
definitions.partially-predicted, totally-predicted,: A reference gene can be either unpredicted or 'predicted'. It's considered predicted when at least one of its cds nucleotides from any of its transcripts was found in the candidate prediction. The reference transcript of the gene that has the most cds nucleotides in common with the candidate prediction is the one used for the comparisons.On the 'predicted' genes, if the candidate prediction is exactly equal to one of the transcripts of the reference prediction, it's considered 'totally-predicted', otherwise it's considered 'partially-predicted'.
definitions.selected-transcript, average-transcript: When a gene is predicted, the 'selected-transcript' is the transcript of the reference that has the most cds nucleotides in common with the prediction from the candidate, the 'average-transcript' use the average of all the possible transcripts of that gene for the calculations.
definitions.recall, precision: Some statistics are calculated using the 'recall' - True Positives/(True Positives + False Negatives) - and precision - True Positives/(True Positives + False Positives). This statistics are made only for the predicted genes. The recall uses the reference predicted transcript against all the others on the reference, and the precision uses the same logic but with the candidate.
definitions.single-exon, multiple-exon, any-quantity: Analyses for predicted genes can be made taking into account only the ones that have the prediction transcript with a 'single-exon', 'multiple-exon' or both - 'any-quantity-exon'. The predicted gene analyzed is the one from the reference if it's the recall or the baseline if is precision.

parameters.description: Percentage of chromosome-strand-groups that have ONLY the predictions from the refence in respect to the ones that contain AT LEAST the predictions from the reference.
Percentage of genes from the reference in which not a single cds nucleotide from any of its transcripts was found in predictions from the baseline.
Percentage of partially-predicted genes that have the first cds nucleotide of the the reference prediction and the first cds nucleotide of the candidate prediction on the same frame.
Average of the ratio of number of exons in the partially-predicted candidate prediction per its reference prediction.
Average of the ratio of number of cds nucleotides in the partially-predicted candidate prediction per its reference prediction.

Percentage of predicted genes that have at least one transcript with intron retention in which the predicted transcript of the reference is the the one with the most, or tied with the most, intron retention occurances out of all the possible transcripts for the predicted gene.
Average size of the exons, in nucleotides, for the predicted genes. In the case of average-transcript is the average size of the exons is the average of the transcripts average size of the exons.

Percentage of predicted transcripts that are single exons. The reference transcripts are analyzed in the case of recall and the candidate ones in the case of precision.
